backrank_1.title: Back-Rank Mate 1
backrank_1.instruction: Black to move — force mate starting with Qe1+, mate in 3 (rated 601).

backrank_1.concept: When a king is hemmed in on the back rank by its own pawns, a rook or queen check along that rank is checkmate — the king has no escape square.
backrank_1.takeaway: Before attacking, check: can the enemy king leave the back rank?

Move 3: Rxe1# — the back-rank mate delivers checkmate. Before attacking, check: can the enemy king leave the back rank?

The key move starts with Qe1+.

backrank_1.explanation: Before attacking, check: can the enemy king leave the back rank? Solutions: Qe1+, Rxe1+, Rxe1#.

advantage_1.title: Converting Advantages 1
advantage_1.instruction: Black to move — win with Nxf4: the conversion in 2 of your moves (rated 1400).
advantage_1.goal: Black to move — win with Nxf4: the conversion in 2 of your moves (rated 1400).
advantage_1.concept: Winning an advantage is half the job. Convert it: improve your worst piece, fix enemy weaknesses, open a second front, and trade into endgames you win — without letting counterplay breathe.
advantage_1.takeaway: Better means: improve, restrict, then collect.
narration: Move 1: Nxf4 — the conversion collects material. Better means: improve, restrict, then collect.
Move 2: Bxg2 — the conversion collects material. Better means: improve, restrict, then collect.
hints: Find your worst piece and improve it while denying counterplay.
The key move starts with Nxf4.
advantage_1.mistakeText: That drifts and lets counterplay in. With an edge, every move should improve or restrict.
advantage_1.explanation: Better means: improve, restrict, then collect. Solutions: Nxf4, Bxg2.
